Definition: from G3167; superbness, i.e. glory or splendor:--magnificence, majesty, mighty power.
BiblicalUsage: Majesty is the splendour of God, and the word is used where men see it and fall back: the crowd is amazed at the mighty power of God when Jesus heals the boy, and Paul warns that Diana's magnificence will be destroyed. Peter says the apostles were eyewitnesses of Christ's majesty on the mount.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe majesty is what happens when the veil lifts: the crowd sees God's power in a healed boy, the silversmith fears for his goddess, and Peter never forgot the mountain. The majesty of Christ is not an idea but a sight, and those who saw it could not keep quiet.
